holidays.name: National Artichoke Hearts Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the tender, tangy center of the artichoke. Celebrate by tossing them into salads, dips, pizzas, or just eating them straight from the jar like a delightfully fancy snack.
holidays.origin: Like many food observances, it comes from the American tradition of unofficial food days promoted by food enthusiasts and marketers. No single founder is firmly documented.
holidays.funFact: The artichoke is actually an unopened flower bud of a thistle plant. If left to bloom, it becomes a giant purple flower.

holidays.name: Freedom of Information Day
holidays.description: A day that champions open government and the public's right to know. It is a nerdy but noble occasion that celebrates transparency, public records, and the joy of a well-timed records request.
holidays.origin: It is observed on March 16, the birthday of James Madison, the fourth U.S. President and a strong advocate of open government and public access to information. The observance has been promoted by transparency and library groups since the late 1980s.
holidays.funFact: Madison wrote that a popular government without popular information is but a prologue to a farce or a tragedy, or perhaps both.

holidays.name: Everything You Think Is Wrong Day
holidays.description: A day for questioning your assumptions, admitting you might be mistaken, and embracing the humbling possibility that your most confident opinions are wrong. Great for gentle arguments and open minds.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, tongue-in-cheek observance that appears on lists of quirky holidays. It encourages people to challenge their beliefs and consider other viewpoints.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists call the tendency to overrate our own correctness overconfidence bias, and it affects nearly everyone, including experts.

holidays.name: Panic Day
holidays.description: A day when you are officially allowed to run around in a tizzy and freak out about everything and nothing. Deadlines, dishes, and dentist appointments are all fair game for dramatic flailing.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, humorous observance from the world of lighthearted calendars, designed to give people a comedic outlet for stress.
holidays.funFact: The word panic comes from Pan, the Greek god of the wild, whose sudden shouts were said to cause irrational fear in travelers and armies.

holidays.name: Lips Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate your smackers, from kissing to smiling to puckering up for a duck-face selfie. Break out the lip balm and give your lips some love.
holidays.origin: This is an informal, social-media-friendly observance popularized by lighthearted holiday calendars and beauty fans.
holidays.funFact: Lips have no oil glands, which is why they get chapped so easily and need extra moisture from balm.
